name: Barnard's Galaxy
tagline: A Local Group irregular in Sagittarius — 1.63 Mly out, a dwarf that looks like a small Magellanic Cloud.

facts.label: H II regions
facts.value: Bright emission knots at its ends

history: Barnard's Galaxy is the Local Group's nearest genuinely isolated irregular — a small gas-rich system in Sagittarius that Edward Emerson Barnard found in 1884. It hosts bright H II regions (including Hubble V) where young massive stars ionize the gas, and its structure resembles a shrunken Magellanic Cloud. Its intermediate-metallicity stars make it a benchmark for how dwarf galaxies evolve outside major-galaxy influence.
